scope: Implement only the accepted MU Desk Dynamic Capture (effect-capture) module, its native short-region capture pipeline, local AI context package, explicit Codex send action, and the minimum host/Quick Ring/settings/tray integration required by the accepted contracts.

owned_files.change: New pure settings model for duration, countdown, output root, optional global hotkey, and Quick Ring assignment defaults.
New package and send-state records with validation, relative paths, timestamps, frame metadata, and no credential fields.
New deterministic selector preserving first/last frames and motion-change peaks while returning 8–16 timestamped frames.
New protocol DTOs and newline-delimited JSON-RPC parsing independent from process I/O.
Add one nested Dynamic Capture settings section without changing existing defaults for startup, Quick Ring, or Desktop Organizer.
Add only keyed capture overlay, HUD, completion, progress, and send-state resources using the accepted inherited tokens.
New on-demand IToolModule coordinator enforcing one active capture, explicit state transitions, cancellation, host errors, and completion-window reuse.
New Windows.Graphics.Capture/Direct3D 11 region frame source with per-monitor DPI conversion, optional cursor capture, and overlay exclusion.
New native H.264 MP4 encoder for short BGRA frames; handle even encoded dimensions while retaining the exact logical crop in metadata and PNG frames.
New atomic temp-to-final package writer for MP4, PNG key frames, contact sheet, effect.md, and send-state.json.
Discover and version-check an official local Codex executable without bundling or downloading one.
Own the stdio app-server process, initialize handshake, account/read and managed login, thread/start, turn/start with text/localImage inputs, streaming, cancellation, and sanitized errors.
Map a validated package to one new read-only Codex task, persist identifiers before success, and resume/check known sends instead of blindly duplicating tasks.
Register only a user-selected non-conflicting hotkey; default is unassigned and failure leaves direct entries usable.
Minimal Windows SDK interop for Direct3D device/surface access, Media Foundation sink writing, capture exclusion, and safe COM/native handle lifetime; no broad native wrapper dependency.
New per-monitor dark-translucent selection overlay with exact cutout, handles, dimensions, keyboard cancellation, and outside-region control placement.
Own physical/logical coordinate mapping, one-monitor selection constraint, drag/resize, countdown, and exclusion of all overlay windows from encoded pixels.
New outside-region recording HUD with text/dot/timer, Stop, Cancel, scaling, and edge flipping.
Update real elapsed/total time, route stop/cancel, and preserve no-HUD-inside-capture geometry.
New light-outlined processing/completion surface with still preview, ordered timestamped key-frame strip, consent summary, Send to Codex primary action, folder, retry, and re-record actions.
Drive processing, preview, sign-in, send, success/failure, retry, reduced motion, focus, and safe-close states.
New MU Desk-owned settings surface containing Dynamic Capture duration, countdown, output location, optional hotkey, and Quick Ring assignment; it is not a separately branded module window.
Validate output location and hotkey conflicts, save atomically through the shared store, and expose reset without deleting captures or Codex auth.
Move the shared target to %LocalAppData%/MU Desk/settings.json through a copy-only atomic migration from %LocalAppData%/PersonalToolbox/settings.json; never delete the legacy file.
Add one Dynamic Capture command and hidden-window Codex completion/failure notifications without a second tray icon.
Construct and wire EffectCaptureModule, host entries, settings, shutdown confirmation, errors, and in-flight Codex lifecycle while preserving single-instance behavior.
Add the accepted Dynamic Capture card and MU Desk settings entry without restyling or reordering unrelated module behavior.
Route Start Capture and shared Settings actions and refresh on-demand module state.
Add EffectCapture as a hosted-only action value while preserving every existing serialized enum value.
Expose Dynamic Capture only when Mouse Ring is hosted by MU Desk; do not present a broken action in the standalone compatibility app.
Accept a host-provided callback for Dynamic Capture while preserving all existing Windows actions.
Register/invoke the host callback and keep standalone behavior compatible.
Use the hosted action catalog so Dynamic Capture can be assigned only inside MU Desk.
Draw the approved code-native selection-corners/frames glyph for the new action.
New approved module icon exports at 16, 20, 24, 32, 64, 128, and 256 px.
Package Effect Capture icon resources and required Windows interop settings; do not add FFmpeg or a second Codex runtime.
Add deterministic settings migration, key-frame selection, package validation, atomic commit, send-state, JSON-RPC parsing, and sanitized-error tests.
Verify existing enum serialization remains stable and the hosted-only Dynamic Capture action is absent from standalone choices.

technical_route.capture: Windows.Graphics.Capture monitor frames cropped to one selected monitor-local rectangle; Direct3D 11 surfaces with Windows 10 2004+ capture-exclusion for MU overlay/HUD windows.
technical_route.video: Native Media Foundation H.264 MP4 at a nominal cadence suitable for 60 fps short UI motion; no audio and no FFmpeg.
technical_route.images: Exact logical crop PNG frames; representative poster and contact sheet built locally from selected frames.
technical_route.key_frames: First/last plus luminance/edge motion-change peaks with minimum temporal spacing, returning 8–16 ordered timestamps; never discard source.mp4.
technical_route.codex: Official codex app-server stdio JSON-RPC with Codex-managed ChatGPT auth, one new read-only package-scoped thread, then text and localImage turn inputs.
technical_route.runtime_weight: No idle capture worker, encoder, model runtime, FFmpeg bundle, browser engine, database, or independent updater.

preserve: MU Desk remains the single process, user entry, tray, startup item, settings owner, version, About surface, and package.
Quick Ring, Cursor Gallery, Desktop Organizer, VPet compatibility, single-instance activation, startup behavior, and existing tray actions continue to work.
Every existing Mouse Ring enum numeric value and saved direction assignment remains compatible.
Existing Toolbox settings migrate by copy and are not deleted, reset, or silently replaced by defaults.
No capture, encoder, frame analyzer, or Codex child process exists while Dynamic Capture is idle.
A failed or cancelled Codex send never deletes or corrupts a completed local package.
No API key, OAuth token, cookie, captured OCR text, image bytes, or prompt body is written to MU Desk logs or settings.
migrations: When the target is absent and %LocalAppData%/PersonalToolbox/settings.json exists, atomically copy it, deserialize with defaults for new Dynamic Capture fields, and leave the source untouched.
When shared settings migration fails, continue reading the legacy settings without reporting a successful target migration; do not overwrite either file.
Create the Dynamic Capture output root lazily on the first capture, not at application startup.
Do not migrate, move, index, or delete arbitrary user video/image folders.
implementation_sequence: Add pure settings/package/send-state/JSON-RPC/key-frame core models and deterministic tests, including copy-only shared-settings migration.
Implement the minimal native capture interop and prove one 2-second monitor-local region can produce ordered BGRA frames without capturing the overlay.
Implement Media Foundation MP4 encoding plus PNG/key-frame/contact-sheet/effect.md atomic package creation and validate 2, 5, and 7 second packages.
Build the selection overlay, countdown, recording HUD, processing/completion window, state machine, cancellation, DPI handling, keyboard flow, and reduced-motion behavior.
Add EffectCaptureModule and wire the MU Desk card, shared settings surface, tray entry, optional global hotkey, shutdown confirmation, and unified errors.
Extend hosted Mouse Ring with the Dynamic Capture action while keeping standalone catalogs and existing serialized assignments compatible.
Implement Codex executable discovery and the JSON-RPC app-server client against a deterministic fake process before using a real account.
Implement managed login, package-scoped read-only thread creation, text/localImage turn submission, streaming, send-state persistence, retry, and hidden-window notifications.
Produce the approved module icon family, run small-size QA, and integrate it only into accepted placements.
Run clean build/tests, package/publish checks, visual/accessibility checks, controlled native capture checks, one explicit real Codex send, recovery checks, and record evidence in acceptance.md.

risks.risk: Overlay or HUD pixels could contaminate the selected recording.
risks.mitigation: Set capture exclusion on every MU overlay/HUD window, place controls outside the logical crop, test a high-contrast HUD over the target, and fail the acceptance check if any control appears in MP4 or PNG frames.

risks.risk: WPF logical coordinates, per-monitor DPI, negative desktop coordinates, and GPU pixel coordinates can disagree.
risks.mitigation: Keep the selected rectangle on one originating monitor, convert through that monitor's DPI transform once, store physical coordinates, and test 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling including a monitor left of the primary display.

risks.risk: H.264 encoders require even dimensions while the user can select an odd-sized region.
risks.mitigation: Keep PNGs and manifest at exact logical size, pad only the encoded edge to even dimensions, and record logical and encoded dimensions separately.

risks.risk: A very fast overshoot or easing turn could be absent from uniformly sampled key frames.
risks.mitigation: Capture at high cadence, score consecutive-frame change, preserve local motion peaks plus endpoints, enforce time spacing only after peak ranking, and always retain source.mp4.

risks.risk: GPU/Media Foundation resource leaks could keep the desktop or encoder busy after closing.
risks.mitigation: Use explicit disposable ownership, cancellation-safe finally blocks, frame-pool shutdown before device disposal, and process/resource counts in repeated-capture acceptance tests.

risks.risk: The installed Codex app-server protocol or executable location may differ from the tested version.
risks.mitigation: Discover/version-check at send time, implement only the documented stable stdio surface, parse unknown notifications defensively, and leave local capture fully usable when incompatible.

risks.risk: Child-process stdout/stderr backpressure or a partial JSON line could deadlock the UI.
risks.mitigation: Use asynchronous independent readers, bounded event dispatch, newline framing with partial-line buffering, cancellation timeouts, and a fake noisy app-server test.

risks.risk: A timeout after thread creation could create duplicate Codex tasks on retry.
risks.mitigation: Persist thread and turn identifiers immediately, distinguish unknown/accepted/completed states, and resume/check known identifiers before allowing a new send.

risks.risk: Captured frames may contain sensitive information.
risks.mitigation: Keep capture local until an explicit click, show exact send count and disclosure, allow folder inspection, restrict the Codex task to the package, and exclude media/prompt content from logs.

risks.risk: Shared settings migration or Quick Ring changes could regress existing modules.
risks.mitigation: Copy rather than move, preserve enum numeric values, default new fields during deserialization, test legacy fixtures, and run all Toolbox/MouseRing/DesktopOrganizer suites.

build: Release build and all Toolbox, MouseRing, and DesktopOrganizer tests pass from a clean process start.
Published output contains MU Desk and approved assets but no FFmpeg executable, API key, auth token, or standalone Dynamic Capture executable.
core_tests: Legacy PersonalToolbox settings copy atomically to MU Desk and retain all existing values; source remains untouched.
Malformed or blocked settings migration reports a real error and does not overwrite either file.
Key-frame selection returns ordered 8–16 frames, always includes first/last, retains a synthetic overshoot peak, and behaves deterministically.
Package validation rejects missing MP4, missing frame, unsafe relative paths, wrong timestamps, and incomplete temp directories.
Atomic package commit leaves no successful-looking final directory on simulated write failure.
Codex JSON-RPC parser handles fragmented lines, unknown notifications, error responses, login events, turn identifiers, completion, cancellation, and malformed JSON.
Known thread state prevents duplicate creation after a simulated response timeout.
Sanitized diagnostics omit prompts, image bytes, absolute captured titles, and credential-shaped values.
All existing Mouse Ring action numeric values remain unchanged and Dynamic Capture is offered only in hosted mode.
capture_flow: Launch from the MU Desk card, tray, and assigned Quick Ring direction; all activate one capture operation.
Select a 320x180 region on each available monitor at 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling; verify exact physical crop and no cross-monitor coordinate drift.
Record 2, 5, and 7 second samples; verify Stop, Cancel, Esc, countdown, timer, re-record, and close behavior.
Use a high-contrast overlay/HUD over the target and verify neither appears in MP4, PNG frames, poster, or contact sheet.
Capture a 100–200 ms scale/opacity overshoot at high cadence and verify start, motion peak, overshoot, settle, and end frames remain ordered with timestamps.
Select odd width/height and verify PNG dimensions are exact, MP4 plays, and logical versus encoded dimensions are recorded.
Repeat capture/cancel/send cycles and verify no persistent GPU, encoder, app-server, overlay, or child-process leak remains.
package_and_privacy: A completed folder contains playable source.mp4, contact-sheet.png, 8–16 valid PNG frames, effect.md, and send-state.json.
Before Send, monitor network/process behavior and verify no Codex process or network submission occurs.
Completion copy shows the real frame count and states that MP4 remains local.
Changing output root affects new packages only; reset preserves all completed packages.
Temporary directories older than 24 hours are cleaned only when positively identified as incomplete module workspaces.
Logs contain sanitized stage metadata and never include captured content or credentials.
codex_integration: Run against a fake app-server that exercises initialize, initialized, account/read, managed-login events, thread/start, turn/start with text/localImage, streaming, success, failure, cancellation, and timeout.
With Codex absent or incompatible, local capture remains usable and Send shows a concrete unavailable/version error.
With authentication absent, Connect Codex starts the managed flow and cancelled login sends nothing.

Perform one explicit real send using a dedicated non-sensitive test package; verify a new thread and first turn identifiers are stored and the submitted input contains the prompt plus ordered localImage frames.
Verify source.mp4 is not attached as an image input and no unrelated workspace is writable by the new task.
Close the completion window during the controlled send; verify the task continues, one tray result appears, and retry does not create a known duplicate.
accessibility_and_visual: Inspect light completion/settings surfaces and dark selection/HUD surfaces against the accepted tokens and no-override contract.
Keyboard can cancel selection, activate duration/Start/Stop/Send/folder/retry actions, traverse key frames, and retain visible focus.
Selection, recording, sending, success, and failure are distinguishable without color.
At 200% scaling, the HUD flips instead of clipping, the completion panel reflows without page-level horizontal scrolling, and text remains readable.
Reduced motion removes eased countdown/preview transitions and the clip does not autoplay indefinitely.
The final icon remains legible at 16, 20, 24, and 32 px and uses the accepted selection-corners/frames metaphor.
system_and_recovery: There is one MU Desk process, tray icon, startup entry, settings owner, version, and installer artifact.
Idle MU Desk has no capture, encoder, analyzer, Codex app-server, or Dynamic Capture child process.
A second invocation activates the existing selection/recording/processing surface instead of creating a second operation.
Exit during recording or send requires confirmation; confirmed exit preserves a completed local package and releases native/process resources.
Capture failure, disk-full simulation, missing frame, login failure, service error, and rate-limit error remain visible and never display success.
Quick Ring, Cursor Gallery, Desktop Organizer, startup, single-instance activation, tray pause/exit, and legacy settings still pass representative smoke paths.

rollback_and_recovery: All new user data is isolated under the accepted Effect Capture root and no existing capture or legacy settings file is deleted.
If native capture initialization fails, disable only the active capture attempt, keep MU Desk and every other module operational, and expose the actual error.
If Codex integration fails, keep Send unavailable/retryable without disabling recording or local packaging.
If shared settings migration fails, use the readable legacy settings for the session and do not claim the MU Desk target was established.
Removing the new module wiring from a future build leaves completed package folders readable as ordinary MP4, PNG, and Markdown files.
